About

I'm William, an academic librarian at a theological school. I studied Koine Greek and Hebrew at the graduate level and wrote my thesis on λύπη (lupē): grief as a productive, transformative force in the letters of Paul.

Via Lupe grew out of that work. Its conviction is simple: that the heart of Christ's way is radical love and hospitality toward self, neighbor, stranger, enemy, and God, and that grief, the weight of living in time, is something we can welcome in one another rather than hide.

I'm not here to argue anyone into or out of anything. These are notes shared, not verdicts handed down. Most pieces follow the readings of the church year, and some are small moments, word studies, or time spent with older voices in the tradition.

New writing arrives every other Sunday.
